'''Francisco Dean Toste''' (born 1971) is the Gerald E. K. Branch Distinguished Professor of [[Chemistry]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and faculty scientist at the chemical sciences division of [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|Lawrence Berkeley National Lab]]. He is a prominent figure in the field of [[organic chemistry]] and is best known for his contributions to [[gold]] chemistry<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Johansson|first1=Magnus J.|last2=Gorin|first2=David J.|last3=Staben|first3=Steven T.|last4=Toste|first4=F. Dean|date=2005-12-01|title=Gold(I)-Catalyzed Stereoselective Olefin Cyclopropanation|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja0552500|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=127|issue=51|pages=18002–18003|doi=10.1021/ja0552500|pmid=16366541|issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and [[asymmetric ion-pairing catalysis]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hamilton|first1=Gregory L.|last2=Kang|first2=Eun Joo|last3=Mba|first3=Miriam|last4=Toste|first4=F. Dean|date=2007-07-27|title=A Powerful Chiral Counterion Strategy for Asymmetric Transition Metal Catalysis|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1145229|journal=Science|language=en|volume=317|issue=5837|pages=496–499|doi=10.1126/science.1145229|issn=0036-8075|pmid=17656720|bibcode=2007Sci...317..496H|s2cid=14368583|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Toste was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]] in 2015,<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Dean Toste |url=https://rsc-src.ca/en/user/2590/contact |website=Royal Society of Canada |access-date=27 May 2026}}</ref>, member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2018, <ref>{{Cite web|title=F. Dean Toste|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/f-dean-toste|access-date=2021-05-24|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref> Fellow of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2020,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428010617/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 28, 2020|title=2020 NAS Election}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=F. Dean Toste|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/f-dean-toste-wppnsg/|access-date=2021-05-24|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> and a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2026/05/new-fellows-announcement-2026/ |website=The Royal Society |date=27 May 2026 |access-date=27 May 2026}}</ref>

== Education and training ==
F. Dean Toste was born in [[Terceira]], Azores, Portugal in 1971. He attended the [[University of Toronto]] for his undergraduate and masters studies in the group of Ian Still.<ref>{{Cite book|title=The total synthesis of varacin: novel applications of thiocyanate in organic synthesis (M.Sc. Thesis)|last=Toste|first=Francisco Dinarco|publisher=University of Toronto|year=1995|isbn=0612075486}}</ref> With Still, Toste developed several novel reactions of thiocyanates<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Toste|first1=F. Dean|last2=Stefano|first2=Vittorio De|last3=Still|first3=Ian W. J.|date=2006-09-23|title=A Versatile Procedure for the Preparation of Aryl Thiocyanates Using N-Thiocyanatosuccinimide (NTS)|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00397919508012691|journal=Synthetic Communications|volume=25|issue=8|pages=1277–1286|language=en|doi=10.1080/00397919508012691|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1995-04-24|title=Thiocyanate as a versatile synthetic unit: Efficient conversion of ArSCN to aryl alkyl sulfides and aryl thioesters|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/004040399500445I|journal=Tetrahedron Letters|language=en|volume=36|issue=17|pages=2949–2952|doi=10.1016/0040-4039(95)00445-I|issn=0040-4039|last1=Toste|first1=F.Dean|last2=Laronde|first2=Frank|last3=Still|first3=Ian W.J.|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1995-06-19|title=Preparation of t-butyl sulfides by a novel ligand-transfer reaction of aryl thiocyanates|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/004040399500798H|journal=Tetrahedron Letters|language=en|volume=36|issue=25|pages=4361–4364|doi=10.1016/0040-4039(95)00798-H|issn=0040-4039|last1=Toste|first1=F.Dean|last2=Still|first2=Ian W.J.|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Still|first1=Ian W. == Independent career ==
Toste joined the faculty at [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]] in 2002 as an assistant professor. He was promoted to associate professor in 2006, and professor in 2009. In 2017, Toste was appointed the Gerald E. K. Branch Distinguished Professor. He has served as a faculty scientist at the chemical sciences division of [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|Lawrence Berkeley National Lab]] since 2007.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Dean Toste CV (2020)|url=http://www.cchem.berkeley.edu/toste/Toste_CV_2020.pdf}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Toste is the recipient of numerous awards for his work, including the [[Janssen Pharmaceuticals|Janssen]] Prize for Creativity in Organic Synthesis in 2018,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Janssen Prize for Creativity in Organic Synthesis - Prof. F. D. Toste|url=https://www.janssenprizeorganicsynthesis.com/prof-f-d-toste.html|access-date=2021-05-24|website=www.janssenpharmaceuticaprize.com|language=en}}</ref> the [[Humboldt Research Award]] in 2016,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Dean Toste recipient of prestigious Humboldt Research Award {{!}} College of Chemistry|url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/news/professor-dean-toste-recipient-prestigious-humboldt-research-award|access-date=2021-05-24|website=chemistry.berkeley.edu}}</ref> the [[List of Royal Society of Chemistry medals and awards|Catalysis in Organic Chemistry Award]] from the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 2018, and the [[American Chemical Society]] [[List of American Chemical Society national awards|Cope Scholar and E. J. Corey Awards]].<ref name=":0" />
